info.summary: The developer. Assigns the task, approves risky actions, reviews the pull request, and can step in at any point.
info.example: Approves the push, then asks for different copy in review.

info.summary: What starts the loop: an issue, a ticket, or a typed prompt. It becomes the first message in the context window.
info.example: Issue #482, with its stack trace.

info.summary: Everything the model sees on a turn, and the only thing it sees. Anything meant to influence the model has to get in here.
The agent's built-in instructions: how to behave and how to use the tools.
info.example: Never run destructive commands without asking.

info.summary: The name, description and input schema of every tool the model may call. A vague description leads to a misused tool.
info.example: `grep`: search file contents by pattern. Inputs: pattern, path.

info.summary: `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`, loaded at the start of a session: how to build and test, and what to avoid.
info.example: Run `pnpm test`. Add no new dependencies.

info.summary: Packaged instructions. Only a short description of each skill sits in context; the full instructions load when a task needs them.
info.example: The `add-export-route` skill, loaded for the CSV ticket.

info.summary: Every earlier message in the session: the task, the model's replies, tool calls, and human comments.
The output of each tool call, added after the call. This is how the model learns what happened.
info.example: `grep`: 3 callers of `formatEmailDomain()`.

info.summary: Notes kept on disk between sessions. Loaded into context at the start; the agent updates them through a tool.
info.example: Saved: empty email shows "No email on file".

info.summary: The model. One input, the context window; one output, text and tool calls. It runs nothing itself.
info.example: Replies: read `ProfileCard.tsx`, then `grep email.domain`.

info.summary: The agent's runtime, and the hub. It builds the context, calls the model, runs the tool calls, adds the results, and decides when to stop.
info.example: One turn: call the model, run its two tool calls, add the results, call it again.

info.summary: Builds each turn's context from the system prompt, instructions, memory, history and tool results.
When the context nears its limit, older turns are summarized to make room. Detail can be lost.
info.example: Early exploration condensed into one paragraph.

info.summary: Scripts the agent loop runs on events, such as before a tool call or after an edit. A hook can block the call, or feed its output back to the model.
info.example: After each edit: `tsc --noEmit`.

info.summary: A plan the model keeps up to date through a tool, so the human can follow along and redirect.
info.example: 1. Null-safe helper  2. Hide the row  3. Add a test

info.summary: Snapshots of the files before edits, so a bad change can be rolled back.
info.example: Rolled back after the architecture check failed.

info.summary: When the loop ends: the task is done, or a limit is hit, such as maximum turns, cost or retries.
info.example: After 3 failed attempts, it stops and reports back.

info.summary: Checks every tool call before it runs. Allowed calls run, some wait for a human, and a denial goes back to the model as a tool result.
Allow, ask and deny rules for each tool, set by the user or the project.
info.example: Allow: read, `grep`. Ask: `git push`. Deny: `rm -rf`.

info.summary: Calls that need a person wait here until approved or rejected.
info.example: `git push origin fix/482`: approve?

info.summary: What the agent can do. The model requests a call; the agent loop runs it and adds the result to the context window.
Returns a file's contents.
info.example: `ProfileCard.tsx`, lines 30 to 60.

info.summary: Writes a change to a file in the working tree.
info.example: `formatEmailDomain()` now returns null for a missing email.

info.summary: Finds usages and files across the repo, with `grep` and glob.
info.example: `grep email.domain`: 3 matches.

info.summary: Runs a command in the environment: tests, builds, `git` and other CLIs.
info.example: `gh run view --log-failed`

info.summary: Fetches a web page or document the task needs, if network access is allowed.
info.example: The date-lib v3 migration guide.

info.summary: Tools that external systems expose through the Model Context Protocol.
info.example: Query error tracking for new issues since the deploy.

info.summary: Starts a subagent with its own context window and a narrower task.
info.example: Search `src/admin/` for callers.

info.summary: Type-aware actions from the language server: definitions, references, rename, extract function.
info.example: Go to definition: `exportCustomersCsv`.

info.summary: Scripted transforms that change many files in exactly the same way.
info.example: String SQL rewritten to `qb.select()` in 3 files.

info.summary: Separate agents, each with its own context window. They return a short summary, which keeps the main context clean.
info.example: Its summary said no other callers. It missed one, and the type check caught it.

info.summary: Where tool calls run: an isolated copy of the repo with its own branch, runtime and limits.
A second checkout of the same repo, used only for this task.
The branch the change lives on, kept apart from main until merged.
The fixed runtime: operating system, language and tool versions.
info.example: Node 22 and pnpm 9, while CI also tests Node 20.

info.summary: Operating-system limits on which files, network and processes a command can reach.
info.example: Writes only inside the worktree; network off.

info.summary: The packages installed for this worktree.
A long-running process the agent can test its change against.
info.example: `localhost:3000`, screenshotted at three widths.

info.summary: The repository: the working tree the edits land in, and its `git` history.
Checks that report on a change after it is made. Their output reaches the model as tool results or hook output.
info.example: The type check fails, and the agent fixes the caller it missed.

info.summary: Unit and integration tests. The most direct check that behaviour is right.
Static rules for style and common bugs. A good lint message includes the fix, so the agent knows what to change.
info.example: `no-server-import`: move this into shared/.

info.summary: The compiler's type check.
info.example: `UserTable.tsx:88`: string expected, got null.

info.summary: Rules about structure, such as layers and forbidden imports, enforced as checks instead of review comments.
info.example: Client code may not import server modules.

info.summary: Pattern rules for security issues and common bugs.
info.example: SQL built by string concatenation.

info.summary: A separate model that reviews the diff for problems rules cannot catch.
info.example: Found nothing wrong, though a column was missing.

info.summary: A model that scores output against a rubric.
info.example: Does the PR description match the diff?

info.summary: The same checks on a clean remote machine, triggered by the pull request. The agent reads its logs through a CLI.
info.example: Fails on Node 20 only; the container uses Node 22.

info.summary: The reviewable unit: the branch proposed for merge. Opening it triggers CI and a human review.
Scheduled agent runs, separate from any task, that scan for drift and open small fix PRs.
info.example: A PR removing one unused import.

info.summary: A pre-production deploy. It is not a signal itself; it produces the logs, metrics and errors the agent can query.
Request and application logs from a deploy, queried through a tool.
info.example: 500s only when `tax_region` is empty.

info.summary: Latency, error rates and traces from a deploy, queried through a tool.
info.example: Checkout p95 latency unchanged.

info.summary: Grouped exceptions with stack traces. Queried through a tool, or an alert can open a task on its own.
info.example: 212 events an hour from `InvoiceSerializer`.
